note.explanation: Group 1 metals become more reactive as you go down the group because their atoms get larger, so the outer electron is easier to lose. They also become softer, their melting points decrease, and their densities generally increase.
examples: Lithium reacts steadily with water, while sodium reacts vigorously and potassium reacts violently.
The melting point falls from lithium (180 °C) to caesium (28 °C).
note.checkAnswer: Potassium reacts more vigorously than sodium because it loses its outer electron more easily.
note.simple: Going down Group 1, the atoms get bigger. Their outer electron is easier to remove, so the metals react more strongly.
note.checkQuestion: Why does reactivity increase down Group 1?
note.title: Group 1: the alkali metals
steps: Remember that Group 1 atoms have one electron in their outermost shell.
As you go down the group, atomic size increases.
The outer electron becomes easier to lose.
Therefore, reactivity increases down the group.
Also remember the physical trends: metals get softer, melting points decrease, and density generally increases.
note.answer: Group 1 elements are called alkali metals. Down the group, reactivity and density generally increase, while melting point decreases and the metals become softer.

explain.title: Group 1 elements have one outermost-shell electron
explain.body: All the elements present in group 1 have ns¹ configuration in their outermost shells. They are also called alkali metals. Because the single outer electron can be removed easily, these metals are very reactive. Hydrogen is the exception: it is a gas and a non-metal.

explain.title: Reactivity increases down Group 1
explain.body: Atomic size increases down the group. The outer electron is then easier to lose, so the lower members are more reactive. For example, lithium reacts steadily with water, sodium vigorously and potassium violently.

explain.title: The metals become softer and their melting points decrease
explain.body: Increasing atomic size weakens the interatomic attraction of the atoms in the metals. The metals become softer down the group, and their melting points decrease.

explain.title: Density generally increases down the group
explain.body: Both atomic size and mass increase down the group. The increase in mass is greater than the increase in volume, so density, defined as mass per unit volume, increases gradually down the group.

explain.title: The textbook's definition and trends
explain.body: “relatively soft metals with general trends down the group limited to decreasing melting point, increasing density and increasing reactivity.”

mistakes: Do not say that Group 1 reactivity decreases down the group; it increases.
Do not confuse the physical trends: melting point decreases, while density generally increases.
When explaining softness, include the reason: increasing atomic size weakens interatomic attraction.
Do not describe lithium, sodium and potassium as reacting with water at the same rate.
Remember that the Group 1 metals react with chlorine with increasing vigour down the group.
